name: Sovereign Fuel OS — The M.O.E. Group

items: 3 caps Aloe + 300 ml warm water (coats the stomach before tea or shake)
Collagen: 2 spoons (10 g); 1 scoop micro-dose only with active swelling
3 flat spoons F1 + 2 scoops F3 + 1 scoop Active Fiber Complex in 400 ml cold water (never hot)
About 145 kcal, 19-20 g protein, 15 g carbs, 9 g sugar, 8 g fibre, 1 g fat, GI 15-23
Pills with breakfast: Multivitamin, Calcium, Celactivo (2 a day: breakfast and lunch); Omega-3 and Garlic if prescribed
If Magic Number is 1500+: 3-4 boiled egg whites after the shake
No red meat (beef, lamb, pork) in Phase 1
Pills with lunch: Multivitamin, Calcium, Celactivo
1 tsp Tea in 500 ml warm water, sipped over 30 minutes (about 170 mg caffeine at 1 tsp)
Optional 1/2 tsp Guarana (about 40 mg); nothing caffeinated after 4:00 pm
Limit sodium and heavy carbs; no energy pills at dinner
Niteworks: 2 scoops (10 g) in 300 ml cold water (if prescribed)
Water to target (0.06 L per kg)
ImmuLift: 1 sachet a day in water (if prescribed)

rules: A shake that carries the full nutrients (F1 + F3 + fibre) is a real meal: the professional's time-saver. Never frame shakes or blended food as the problem. The villain is sugar without protein or fibre (fruit smoothies, sweet drinks, carb-only plates).
Breakfast is the System Anchor Shake. Lunch is always chewed: the Lean Hardware Meal. M.O.E. does not advocate 100% liquid diets.
The 3 pm crash protocol: protein-anchored breakfast shake, a chewed lean lunch, the 4:00 pm tea as the last caffeine, water to target.
Hunger is answered with protein and water (+1 scoop F3), not willpower.

The call to action is: comment START (or OPERATOR). That leads to the FORMOH Audit, a 15-minute Strategy Calibration Call, then the Sovereign Health Protocol (Phase 1: days 1-14; Phase 2: days 15-90).

Public content uses the client-layer claims only: no disease, treatment, detox, toxin, fat-oxidation or 'firewall' claims, and no protocol doses above the label. Mention products by their protocol role unless the source names them.
Never cite the Nutrition Journal 2010 meal-replacement trial as F1 evidence (it tested Medifast), and never quote a % for the afternoon dip without a named study.
